note: Crossover design: each task's paired skill is distilled from a DIFFERENT finding in the same class, never its own. Both traps are real review findings against code written 2026-08-10, so neither can be in training data.

tasks.selection_rule: AUTHORING task: the model implements response_text from a contract-only stub and never sees the grading tests, which are applied afterward. This is the only construction that measures knowledge rather than the ability to read a red assertion. NOTE: the paired skill here IS distilled from this same trap, so this task measures the CEILING (does a directly relevant skill change authoring behavior at all), not transfer. Interpret accordingly.
tasks.prompt: scripts/detect.py has a function `response_text(resp)` whose body raises NotImplementedError. Read its docstring for the contract and implement it. Do not change its signature, and do not modify anything under tests/. When you are done, run `python3 tests/test_detect.py` and make sure you have not broken any test that was passing before your change.

tasks.selection_rule: TRANSFER test: same authoring task, but the paired skill is distilled from a DIFFERENT instance (the truncation-reports-absent bug) and never mentions serialization, escaping or flattening. Measures whether same-class knowledge transfers, not whether a matched answer key helps. Compare against the sf-author-response-text control arm (0/3).
